notes: Three of the seven records a round-54 agent returned. The other four were refused and the reasons are in the research log: MMR (round 52 settled that the junta court's secret-trial conviction of Bo Bo Nge stays on the moves layer only, and this is the same episode); BLZ (a governor pressed out by the prime minister is a move against the bank, which Belize already holds, and round 52 settled that a removal filed as a move does not also count as a corruption case); SDN (The Sentry's finding that supervision 'remains weak' and anti-corruption capacity is 'largely untested' is a characterisation with no episode, no conduct and no finding against any person -- the Finland test -- and the agent had attached a governor's name to it who is accused of nothing in the text); DNK (Rigsrevisionen states it does not audit Nationalbanken in its central-bank capacity, and the Public Accounts Committee's 'very unsatisfactory' verdict is aimed at the Ministry of Finance, with the bank acting as the state's debt manager, so the bank is not the subject of the finding; Denmark stays a confirmed blank). Two edits were made to the three kept: Haiti now says plainly that the source does not tie the investigation to any conduct at the bank, and Armenia's people field now names the subject of the allegation rather than the accuser.

records.summary: Pierre Laporte, who left the governorship of the Central Bank of Seychelles in March 2012 to become finance minister, was accused in an anonymous letter circulated in September 2012 of drawing two salaries at the same time, one from the central bank and one from the government. He denied wrongdoing and said he had negotiated a severance package to offset the lower ministerial pay. The accusation was anonymous and no charge, inquiry or ruling is reported, so it stands as an allegation only.
records.source_title: Former Seychelles governor denies drawing double wage (Central Banking)

records.summary: Venel Joseph, former governor of the Banque de la Republique d'Haiti, was barred from leaving the country in April 2004 by justice minister Bernard Gousse, who named him among 37 former officials to be kept available for investigations into crimes allegedly committed by the government of ousted president Jean-Bertrand Aristide. The minister described the travel ban as an insurance policy. The source states that he was named in that group as a former official of the Aristide government and does not say what conduct at the central bank, if any, was under investigation, and reports no charge and no finding.
records.source_title: Ex-cb chief banned from leaving Haiti (Central Banking)

records.category: conflict of interest in ownership of a commercial bank
records.people: Central Bank of Armenia, through Housing for Young Families, a refinancing credit organisation it founded
records.summary: In February 2022 Armbusinessbank's new ownership was registered as MFM Global Invest LLC of Switzerland with 74.998 per cent and Housing for Young Families, a refinancing credit organisation founded by the Central Bank of Armenia, with 25.001 per cent. Former labour minister Maneh Tandilyan publicly called the deal non-transparent and a gross violation of the law barring the regulator from interfering in the activities of commercial banks, and the central bank gave no comment to the news agency. The allegation rests on that one named former official's public statement, no inquiry or ruling is reported, and it stands as a claim rather than a finding.
records.source_title: 'Mysterious' deal in Armenian banking sector or how Central Bank became shareholder of commercial bank (ArmBanks)
